body_ar: غرق الكثير من المسلمين اليوم في محيط الغفلات المتلاطم، فضيعوا الواجبات، واجترءوا على المحرمات، ونسوا الله والدار الآخرة، ولم ينج من الغرق إلا من ركب قوارب النجاة التي تصنعها الخشية من الله ومراقبته وذكره، فالخائف من الله قوي الإيمان في كل مواجهة مع الشيطان، وثيق الصلة بربه الكريم الرحمن، لا تلقاه إلا حيث أراد الله، لأنه موقن أن الله معه يسمعه ويراه، ومن كان هذا حاله فإن الله في الدنيا مولاه، والجنة في الآخرة مأواه. خشية الله ناتجة عن العلم به: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته. أما بعد: فإن من قيم الإيمان التي ينبغي أن يتحلى بها كل مؤمن: خشية الله سبحانه وتعالى، فهو أهل للخشية، ومن حقوقه على عباده أن يخافوه وأن لا يشركوا به شيئاً، وذلك مقتض لتمام معرفته، فمن عرف الله تعالى خافه، وقد بين الله سبحانه وتعالى سر هذه الخشية، فربطه بالعلم، فقال تعالى: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ. [فاطر:28]...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Many Muslims today have drowned in the surging ocean of heedlessness, so that they have neglected the obligations, made bold against the forbidden things, and forgotten God and the abode of the hereafter. None has been saved from drowning except one who has boarded the lifeboats built by the fear of God, by awareness of His watching, and by the remembrance of Him. For one who fears God is strong in faith in every encounter with Satan, and firmly bound to his Lord, the Generous, the All-Merciful; you will not meet him except where God willed him to be, because he is certain that God is with him, hearing him and seeing him. Whoever is in this condition — God is his protector in this world, and the Garden is his dwelling in the hereafter.

## The fear of God arises out of knowledge of Him

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and God's mercy and His blessings. To proceed:

Among the values of faith with which every believer ought to adorn himself is the fear of God, glorified and exalted is He; for He is worthy to be feared, and it is among His rights over His servants that they fear Him and that they associate nothing with Him. That requires the completeness of knowing Him, for whoever has come to know God Most High fears Him. God, glorified and exalted is He, has made plain the secret of this fear, binding it to knowledge, for He said, exalted is He: {It is only those of His servants who have knowledge that fear God.} [Fāṭir 28]...

flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis at the proof-text, before anything is built on it; this is also the only record in the run whose download is a .docx rather than a .doc. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/c-a-17.docx. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.context: the two ruling terms, in the plural, inside the site's synopsis
options: the obligations / the forbidden things, by the fixed mapping
flags.note: The two ruling categories appear here in the plural and as substantives, and the fixed renderings are used. Note the attribution: both fall inside the site's synopsis, not in the Sheikh's transcribed words, and the charge that many Muslims today neglect the obligations and make bold against the forbidden is the site editor's, not his. Nothing in the transcribed portion grades anything.

flags.context: the two roots for fear used throughout the record
options: render khashyah as 'fear of God' and khawf as 'fear', keeping the pair distinct where possible
use a single English word for both
flags.note: The record moves between khashyah, which is awe arising from knowledge of the one feared, and khawf, plain fear — and its whole argument is that the first arises from knowledge, which is why the proof-text chosen has 'those of His servants who have knowledge'. English has no matching pair, and this rendering uses 'fear' for both while letting the argument carry the distinction. A reviewer may prefer 'awe' for khashyah; if so it must be changed consistently, including in the title.

translator_notes: One of a run of thirteen records, IDs 688-700, all uploaded on 5 and 8-9 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-a-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lessons were delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.
The transcribed portion opens with a greeting to an audience, which marks it as a lesson delivered to people present.
The Qur'anic rendering is interpretive and is not a substitute for the Arabic; the source's own bracket reference style has been kept.
'واجترءوا' is written with a free-standing hamza for 'واجترأوا'; left as served.
